label: Filing & payment
question: For tax year 2025, I am an individual calendar-year taxpayer. I obtained a six-month extension to file my federal income tax return, but have not paid the tax. Does the filing extension also extend the payment deadline? Separate what can be established from what needs more facts.
title: Does filing later mean paying later?

walkthrough.explanation: The pinned model treats an extension of the filing period and the time for payment as separate issues. To apply those rules to you, the live conversation needs the relevant year, return and facts about the extension. This walkthrough does not establish a payment date.
missing: Which tax year and type of return are involved?
Was an extension granted, and what does it cover?
What is the original due date, and what payments have been made?
walkthrough.question: Does an extension to file give me more time to pay?

sources.label: 26 U.S.C. §6081(a)
sources.note: Excerpt from a pinned repository artifact; not a current-law verification.
sources.quote:
(a) General rule
The Secretary may grant a reasonable extension of time for filing any return, declaration, statement, or other document required by this title or by regulations. Except in the case of taxpayers who are abroad, no such extension shall be for more than 6 months.

sources.label: 26 U.S.C. §6151(a)
sources.note: Excerpt from a pinned repository artifact; not a current-law verification.
sources.quote:
(a) General rule
Except as otherwise provided in this subchapter, when a return of tax is required under this title or regulations, the person required to make such return shall, without assessment or notice and demand from the Secretary, pay such tax to the internal revenue officer with whom the return is filed, and shall pay such tax at the time and place fixed for filing the return (determined without regard to any extension of time for filing the return).

walkthrough.title: Start by separating filing from payment.

label: IRS notice
question: I received a notice of deficiency for my 2025 federal income tax. It was mailed on March 2, 2026, to my US address. I was physically in Japan when it was mailed, returned on March 20, and have not filed a petition. Is the Tax Court petition window 90 or 150 days? Do not infer the answer from physical presence alone; show the required predicates and facts. Identify anything preventing a definitive deadline.
title: Which deadline applies to my notice?

walkthrough.explanation: Different notices can lead to different procedures. The assessment package contains rules for the petition window following a deficiency notice. A date cannot be established from the phrase “an IRS notice” alone. In live mode, the response should identify the applicable rule and ask for the facts it requires.
missing: Is this a notice of deficiency or a different IRS notice?
On what date was it mailed?
Was the notice addressed to a person outside the United States?
Is there a stated petition deadline or another relevant proceeding?

label: Credits & eligibility
question: For 2025, a married couple filing jointly lived in the US all year, with two children aged 8 and 11 who lived with them all year. They report $32,000 in W-2 wages, $1,000 in bank interest, and a $2,000 recognized capital gain. There is no other income. Can they claim EITC and what amount follows? Do not assume missing eligibility facts, qualifying-child tests or SSN status. If the pinned model cannot execute, say so instead of calculating from memory.
title: Can this household claim EITC?

label: Cross-border income
question: For 2025, a US citizen moved to Germany on February 1. They report $140,000 of employee wages earned while working there, $28,000 of German income tax, a US rental property with $12,000 net income, and 20 workdays physically in the US. They are married to a nonresident alien and made no election. Compare possible foreign earned income exclusion and foreign tax credit treatment, residence/physical presence tests, source of wages, filing status and interactions. Identify missing dates and facts, and do not silently assume a tax treaty or current inflation amounts.
title: Foreign income, residence and credits

label: Corporate transaction
question: In 2025, a domestic C corporation with $8 million of NOL carryforwards and shareholder stock basis of $400,000 transfers assets to another domestic corporation. Shareholders receive acquiring-company shares worth $1.2 million plus $300,000 cash. A 60% ownership change is reported. The transferor distributes all consideration and liquidates. Analyze potential section 368 reorganization classification, section 356 recognition and characterization of boot, section 358 basis, and section 382 limits. Do not assume continuity, business purpose, valuation dates, NOL vintage, loss-corporation status or the applicable federal rate. Separate statutory conditions, judgment questions, missing facts and any execution gaps.
title: Reorganization, boot and loss limits

label: Estate & gift
question: A US citizen died in 2025, survived by a spouse who is not a US citizen. The gross estate is stated as $9 million; adjusted taxable gifts total $2 million; $3 million passes outright to the spouse; a prior spouse left a claimed DSUE amount of $1.5 million. No estate tax return or QDOT election has been filed. Analyze estate-tax computation, marital deduction/QDOT requirements, portability elections and gift/estate interactions. Identify what cannot be concluded without facts or applicable-year parameters. Do not invent a 2025 exemption or assume that claimed DSUE is established.
title: Portability, gifts and a surviving spouse

label: Procedure & limitations
question: For 2022, an individual calendar-year taxpayer obtained a filing extension, filed the original return on October 10, 2023, and paid $10,000 of tax through withholding during 2022 plus $2,000 on April 15, 2023. They filed an amended return claiming a $4,000 refund on September 1, 2026. Bankruptcy proceedings ran from May 1 to November 30, 2024. Determine the section 6511 claim period and lookback issues, whether a filing extension affects each, and whether bankruptcy supplies a relevant suspension under the pinned rules. Do not equate assessment limitation suspension with refund claim suspension. Separate calculations that actually execute from source explanations.
title: Amended return, extension and bankruptcy

label: Partnership interests

question: A partner receives a nonliquidating $30,000 distribution plus property (partnership basis $50,000) when outside basis is $120,000 (T1). Later a $25,000 liability-share decrease with no cash is scoped to T2 (outside basis $40,000 entering T2). The partner then sells the interest for $100,000 cash plus $60,000 of relieved liabilities; $50,000 of the amount realized is attributable to hot assets with $35,000 of basis. Using law as of June 30, 2025: compute T1 gain and after-basis, the combined T2 gain and after-basis (no double path), the carried sale basis, the §752(d) proceeds versus the §741 total gain, and the §751(a) ordinary versus capital split.

question: D1 died in 2025 with portability elected; examination fixed the tentative base at $8,200,000 (as-filed base $8,000,000). The surviving spouse remarried and died in 2026 (D2, $10,000,000 base, portability elected, holding D1 DSUE). The new survivor S died in 2026 with $31,000,000 gross estate, $1,000,000 deductions and $2,000,000 of 2020 taxable gifts. Using the law of each year: compute D1 final DSUE, D2 final DSUE, the DSUE available to S, the applicable exclusion, and the final estate tax after the gift-tax adjustment and unified credit. In 2028 a $2,000,000 QDOT principal distribution (event 1) is made, the first-round tax paid from the trust: compute the first-round tax and the incremental second-round tax.
